label: Person
name: Hermeric
summary:
Hermeric was the Suevi king from at least 406 to his abdication in 438, and possibly as early as 419. He played a significant role in the Western Roman Empire's decline and fragmentation. His reign marked the beginning of the Suevic Kingdom, which lasted until its eventual conquest by the Visigoths in 585.

 Hermeric was born into a noble family and rose to power through a combination of military victories and strategic alliances. He expanded the Suevi kingdom's borders, conquering territories from modern-day Spain and Portugal to parts of France and North Africa. Despite his military successes, Hermeric faced significant challenges, including the constant threat of neighboring tribes and the pressure of maintaining a vast empire.

 After abdicating in 438, Hermeric retired to a monastery, where he spent the remainder of his life in contemplation and prayer. He died in 441 CE, leaving behind a legacy as one of the most influential leaders in Suevi history.

 'The world will never know what we had,' said Hermeric, reflecting on the passing of an era that would soon be lost to the sands of time.
